newsitem.title: USA: NYSE program trading averages 10.4 pct for week.
newsitem.headline: NYSE program trading averages 10.4 pct for week.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said program trading averaged 10.4 percent of its average daily volume of 420.7 million shares, or 43.8 million shares, for the week of September 30 - October 4.
Program trading accounted for an average of 11.7 percent of average daily volume of 430.3 million shares for the week of September 23-27.
Of the average 43.8 million shares during the week, buy programs accounted for an average 23.5 million shares, while sell programs accounted for an average 20.3 million daily.
In all markets, program trading averaged 70.7 million shares a day during the week of September 30 - October 4.

Of the five member firms reporting the most program activity on the New York Stock Exchange, First Options, Lehman Bros., Goldman Sachs and Interactive Brokers executed all or most of its program activity for customers. Morgan Stanley split its program activity between that of its own account and those of its customers.

Program trading executed by firms as agent, for non-member customers, amounted to 65.1 percent during the week, while volume executed as principal, for their own accounts, amounted to 30.7 percent of program volume from September 30 - October 4.

Between September 30 and October 4, 23.3 percent of program trading volume executed by NYSE member firms was related to index arbitrage, while another 12.3 percent involved other derivative product-related strategies.
Program trading encompasses trading strategies involving the sale or purchase of a basket of at least 15 stocks with a value of $1 million or more the exchange said.
